name: Semantic Caching for LLMs
tagline: Cutting LLM latency by 90%+ and GPU token spend via L1 exact-hash lookup + L2 tenant-filtered HNSW vector cache with negation guards.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of semantic LLM caching—from L1/L2 lookup tiers and cosine threshold calibration to negation collisions, cross-tenant pre-filtering, and RAG document invalidation.

spark.summary: Semantic LLM caching intercepts natural-language prompts, embeds them into dense vectors (e.g., 1536-dim via text-embedding-3-small), and performs an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) lookup in a vector store like Redis or Qdrant. When cosine similarity clears a strict threshold (typically 0.93–0.96), the system returns a cached completion in 20–45 ms instead of paying 1.5–6 seconds and $0.01–$0.05 per frontier model inference.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pair an L1 exact-hash cache with an L2 vector ANN cache gated by tenant metadata filters and high cosine thresholds to cut LLM latency by 90%+ without leaking cross-user context.

learningJourney.title: What is Semantic LLM Caching
learningJourney.explanation:
Traditional HTTP/Redis caches require exact byte equality—changing a comma misses `SHA256(prompt)`. **Semantic LLM caching** intercepts natural-language intents (`"How do I reset MFA?"` vs. `"Where can I reconfigure 2FA?"`) using a **two-tier lookup**:

1. **L1 Exact Hash (<2 ms)**: Check `SHA256(normalized_prompt + tenant_id + model_id)`.
2. **L2 Vector ANN (15–40 ms)**: Embed the prompt and run a **pre-filtered** HNSW lookup in Redis Stack or Qdrant; if cosine similarity clears a calibrated threshold (typically **0.93–0.96**) and passes a negation/entity guard, return the cached completion.

cards.detail: Exact normalized SHA-256 hits in <2 ms without paying embedding latency or cost.

cards.label: 2. Pre-Filtered HNSW
cards.detail: Filter tenant_id, role, model_id, and prompt_version inside the vector query—never post-filter.

cards.label: 3. Negation Guard
cards.detail: Verify numbers, flags, and negation tokens ('allow' vs 'block') before serving L2 hits.

sectionDiagram.summary: L1+L2 caching absorbs 25–45% of redundant support/RAG LLM traffic at 20–45 ms p95.

learningJourney.title: Why Naive Cosine Thresholds Fail (Negation & Cross-Tenant Leaks)
learningJourney.explanation: General-purpose bi-encoders compress syntax and semantics into one vector—so **opposite intents score >0.94 cosine similarity**: `'Allow port 443 in AWS SG'` vs. `'Block port 443 in AWS SG'`, or `'delete rows > 100'` vs. `'delete rows < 100'`. Worse, post-filtering a shared vector index risks cross-tenant leaks or zero-hit starvation, and switching embedding models without namespacing corrupts distance comparisons.

learningJourney.title: Where Semantic Caching shines (and where to bypass it)
learningJourney.explanation: Cache deterministic, read-heavy Q&A and documentation bots; bypass caching for personalized stateful queries, high-temperature creative tasks, or tool-calling mutations.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Low-Temperature Support & Docs Q&A ($T \le 0.2$)
benefits: 25–45% cache hit rate slashes GPU spend, stabilizes p95 latency, and shields provider RPM/TPM limits.
costs: Requires golden-set precision/recall calibration on near-miss pairs.

benefits: Bypass cache for `'What is my account balance?'` or `'Summarize my last 10m emails'`.
costs: Serving stale or cross-user state is a correctness and security failure.

comparison.choice: Avoid: High-Temperature Creative & Subtle Code Diffs
benefits: Users expect novel creative outputs, and subtle operator inversions (`>` vs `<`) risk false-positive collisions.
costs: Unless guarded by a cross-encoder or AST verifier, code-diff caching is unsafe.

learningJourney.title: How L1/L2 Lookup, Negation Checks & Doc Invalidation are implemented
learningJourney.explanation: Isolate the normalized user intent (do not embed a 10k-token system prompt), run L1 SHA-256 first, execute pre-filtered L2 ANN, and gate L2 hits < 0.98 with a negation/operator diff or lightweight cross-encoder (`ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`).

options.feedback: Correct: pair cosine thresholds with a negation/entity guard or lightweight cross-encoder before serving L2 hits.

options.feedback: HNSW indexes the full embedding vector; the limitation is in bi-encoder cosine compression.

options.feedback: SHA-256 does not collide on different strings; this happens in L2 vector similarity.
